title: Oscillation mitigation for attention kernel handoff during bursty workloads
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem statement:

We observe an oscillation pattern in the kernel selector under bursty traffic where the runtime repeatedly switches between FlashAttention v2 and v3 variants across adjacent requests. Symptoms include increased p50/p95 latency jitter, transient throughput drops, and occasional OOMs during decoder streams when shape and sequence-length distribution rapidly toggle. This appears tied to:
- aggressive instantaneous scoring in the kernel selector that reacts to per-request metrics without decay
- warmup costs of FlashAttention v3 for certain microbatch/seq_len combinations
- KV cache prefill ordering that interacts with kernel workspace allocation

Goal:
Mitigate oscillation and improve stable tail latency during bursts without regressing average throughput. Provide a guarded rollout plan for a sequenced cooldown and gating strategy that favors stability, with telemetry, safety checks, and rollback hooks.
acceptance_criteria: p95 token-latency under bursty synthetic workload improves or remains stable compared to baseline within 5%
kernel-selection oscillation rate (switches per 1000 requests) reduced by >80% in experiment cluster
no increase in OOM incidence in canary fleet for 48h after rollout
automated telemetry flagging and automatic rollback triggers in place (latency or OOM thresholds)
tasks: Instrument selector telemetry: per-request chosen kernel, selector score history, decision cooldown counters
Create a deterministic prober that exercises FA2/FA3 hot paths for representative seq_len/microbatch combos
Implement cooldown window + exponential backoff in selector to avoid flip-flopping
Add soft gating: prefer last-successful kernel for N requests unless score delta > threshold
Build hedged-fallback path: when switching to FA3, run a lightweight compatibility probe to verify workspace fits before committing
Add prefill-aware workspace reservation heuristic to prevent late OOMs during decode handoffs
Run controlled canary (10% nodes) with synthetic bursty traffic and real-production shadow traffic
Add dashboards and alert rules; wire automatic rollback on p95 regression or OOM spike
Document rollout playbook and add postmortem checklist for any regressions
plan_notes: Week 2: selector cooldown + soft gating implementation + unit tests
Week 3: hedged-fallback + workspace heuristic + integration tests
Week 4: canary rollout, monitor 48h, iterate on thresholds
Follow-up: bake tuned defaults into model profiles and optimize scoring weights
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Too-conservative cooldown could reduce throughput for legitimate workload shifts. Mitigation: parameterize cooldown per-model and expose to runtime profiles for tuning.
Risk: Hedged probes add CPU/GPU overhead. Mitigation: run lightweight probes only during transitions and limit concurrency; measure cost impact in canary.
Risk: Telemetry volume increase. Mitigation: sample non-critical fields and aggregate at agent side; use high-cardinality tags sparingly.
Risk: Interaction with existing rollback automation. Mitigation: coordinate with ops to ensure single canonical rollback source and document precedence rules.
Risk: Edge-case long-context sequences still prefer v2 or v3 incorrectly. Mitigation: include KV-cache prefill-awareness and shape-hash decision cache.
notes: Initial investigation by telemetry team reproduced oscillation in lab with Poisson burst generator (attached traces in confluence).
SRE observed two customer incidents last month that correlate with selector flips during nightly heavy-batching jobs; customer impact flagged P1.
Design doc: lightweight selector state machine + cooldown parameters (link above) — prefer config-driven approach to tune conservatively for enterprise fleets.
Coordination: need signoff from perf, SRE, and product (PM: Elena Rodriguez) before broad rollout.
